public_rationale: Zylo's February 27, 2024 announcement described cautious software purchasing and lower per-employee SaaS spending [e2]. April 2024 reporting priced Slack AI at an additional $10 per user per month and described competing prices, included AI features and vendor-reported benefits [e1, e3]. These records do not establish that declining SaaS spending caused salespeople to have to sell AI add-ons to budget-conscious buyers [e1, e2, e3]. Nor do they supply standards that settle whether those add-ons are 'extremely expensive' or 'equal parts underwhelming and commoditized' [e1, e2, e3]. The pricing and purchasing evidence therefore cannot settle the complete evaluative claim [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: Lower per-employee spending does not establish declining total SaaS spending or the asserted effect on what salespeople must sell [e2].
Reported prices and vendor-reported benefits do not establish excessive cost or representative customer value [e1, e3].
The evidence does not establish practical interchangeability or a measurable meaning for 'equal parts' [e1, e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: With SaaS spend declining, SaaS salespeople are having to sell extremely expensive AI add-ons to budget-conscious decision-makers, and these add-ons are equal parts underwhelming and commoditized.
conditions: as a result of SaaS spend declining

statement.excerpt: As a result, SaaS sales people are having to sell extremely-expensive add-ons to budget-conscious decision-makers, and said add-ons are equal parts underwhelming and commoditized.

our_interpretation: The sentence combines checkable observations about pricing and purchasing conditions with an overall judgment about value.
Extremely expensive has no stated comparator, and underwhelming has no stated performance or customer-value standard.
Equal parts is rhetorical rather than a measurable allocation.
Shared features alone do not establish that products are interchangeable after integration, security and workflow requirements are considered.
No single ordinary empirical rule settles the complete sentence without replacing the author's value judgments.
criteria.support_condition: Not defined for the complete evaluative claim. Prices and budget evidence can establish factual components but cannot establish the overall value judgment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not defined for the complete evaluative claim. A lower price or satisfied customer would not by itself falsify the general judgment.
